project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
A demonstration of technologies for refurbishing existing hydropower plants so they become more efficient, flexible, durable and climate-proof.
The solutions must be socio-economically and environmentally sustainable, including for biodiversity, and the project must assess this.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Scope

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
The call gives an open list of example issues; projects choose which to address, and the call names no excluded activities.
- Innovative design of turbines, draft tubes, nozzles, distributors and generators, based on future load cycles and longer lifetime
- New models and simulation tools for harsher operating conditions, including transient effects of new operating patterns
- Digitalisation and AI for instrumentation, controls, flexibility and new operating strategies that cut operation and maintenance costs
- New materials for efficiency, resistance and lifetime, including phasing out PFAS and mineral oils, and low-greenhouse-gas concrete
- Automated maintenance of metal turbines, reduction of operator hazards and of the cost of electricity linked to operating costs
- Integrated water-use operations and management, simulation and forecasting for climate risk and extreme weather, with full account of biodiversity, good ecological status and fish migration
- Managing water flows and sediment so they do not hamper flexible production, extending the lifetime of concrete structures and improving overtopping safety of embankment and rockfill dams
Every solution must include a socio-economic and environmental sustainability assessment.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Scope

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
A renewables-based power system needs flexible, sustainable hydropower, but the existing fleet must be modernised and adapted to climate change.
The need originates with hydropower operators and the electricity system: plants must deliver more flexibility and stable output alongside variable renewables, face harsher operating conditions and climate impacts, and must meet biodiversity requirements. The call also names the competitiveness of the European hydropower industry.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
Demonstrated refurbishment technologies with a sustainability assessment, plus models, tools and operating strategies for the issues addressed.
The call does not list fixed deliverables; they follow from the issues chosen, for example new turbine designs, simulation and forecasting tools, digital control strategies or new materials, each demonstrated.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Scope

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
Projects must contribute to all three outcomes: a hydropower fleet that better supports a secure grid, a stronger European hydropower industry, and climate-adapted operation.
- Enhance the fleet's ability to provide stable output alongside variable renewables for a secure and stable electricity system, including by modernising grid integration and fleet control
- Increase technology leadership, competitiveness and export potential of the European hydropower industry
- Address climate change adaptation for stable, sustainable operation over the coming decades
The call sets no quantified targets.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Expected Outcome

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The call asks for forward-looking refurbishment solutions and industry competitiveness, but sets no specific replication or uptake duty.
- The granting authority may object, for up to 4 years after the project, to a transfer of ownership or exclusive licensing of results
- The general rule applies that the exploitation and dissemination plan must include a strategy where results become a product, process or service
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 4 · A — Admissibility

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
At least three independent organisations from three different countries; the call sets no maximum.
The general rule requires, as beneficiaries (organisations that sign the grant agreement and receive funding), three legal entities independent of each other: at least one established in an EU Member State and two others each in a different Member State or country associated with Horizon Europe (non-EU countries taking part in the programme, such as Norway, Switzerland or the United Kingdom). Affiliated entities (organisations legally linked to a beneficiary) and associated partners (organisations taking part without funding) do not count towards this minimum.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 13 · B — Eligibility, Consortium composition

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
The call names no required partner types; demonstration in existing plants implies at least one hydropower plant owner or operator.
Entities established in an eligible country but directly or indirectly controlled by China or by a legal entity established in China are not eligible. The need for a plant operator is our reading of the scope.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Specific conditions and Scope

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The call prescribes no division of work or budget.
Since the grant is a lump sum (a fixed amount paid against completed work packages), the consortium must allocate the amount to work packages and partners in a detailed budget table.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, lump sum grant proposals

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
No type of organisation is prescribed: the beneficiaries choose one of themselves as coordinator.
The coordinator manages and coordinates the project and represents the consortium towards the granting authority (the European Commission or its agency). At submission it must confirm that it has the mandate to act for all applicants.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, Submission

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
Formally yes, but TenneT TSO B.V. owns no hydropower plants and has no Dutch hydropower to demonstrate on, so leading would not be credible.
Any eligible beneficiary may coordinate, and a Dutch entity is eligible.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 11, 36 · B — Entities eligible for funding; IMPORTANT, Coordinator
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Scope

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes, as an associated partner, which takes part without funding and bears its own costs.
An associated partner does not sign the grant agreement, cannot charge costs, does not need legal validation and does not count towards the minimum of three beneficiaries from three countries. It must still register in the Participant Register before the application is submitted.
This is the more realistic role for TenneT, for example advising on grid integration requirements.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Eligibility, Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration, Consortium roles and Associated partners
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Yes in principle: as a beneficiary TenneT could receive up to 70% of its eligible costs, paid within a lump sum.
This topic is an innovation action (a project that develops, pilots and demonstrates new or improved solutions close to the market), for which the maximum rate is 70% for organisations other than non-profit legal entities. The grant is a lump sum fixed from a detailed budget and paid against completed work packages. The expected EU contribution is around EUR 8.5 million per project, for the whole consortium. The call sets no Dutch national rules.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Specific conditions

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
TenneT's possible contribution is narrow: grid-integration and flexibility requirements for modernised hydropower, as a TSO perspective in the impact work.
This is our interpretation. One expected outcome is modernised grid integration and fleet control, which is the only point of contact with TenneT. TenneT's experience with flexible access arrangements, such as time-dependent transmission rights, could inform how flexible plants contribute to grid stability. The Netherlands has hardly any hydropower, so a demonstration on TenneT's grid is unlikely; a project would rely on plants in other countries.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Expected Outcome

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer: The solutions must be innovative, such as new designs, materials, tools and operating strategies, demonstrated in refurbishment of existing plants.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Scope

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: Mainly technology (turbines, generators, materials, civil structures) and operational methods (digital control, maintenance and water management).
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Scope

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer: Demonstration of refurbishment solutions, supported by modelling and simulation; not early research.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
Activities are expected to reach TRL 6–7 by the end of the project and may start at any TRL.
TRL 6 is technology demonstrated in a relevant environment; TRL 7 is a system prototype demonstrated in an operational environment.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Specific conditions, Technology Readiness Level
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Technology Readiness Levels

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer: The solutions must be demonstrated for the refurbishment of existing hydropower plants; TRL 6–7 implies a relevant or operational plant environment.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Scope and Specific conditions

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer: Solutions must fit existing plants and the wider water system, and support grid integration and fleet control.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Expected Outcome and Scope

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer: Each solution needs a socio-economic and environmental sustainability assessment, including biodiversity; the call sets no other indicators.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Scope

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer:
The call addresses physical safety of dams and operators, not cybersecurity.
- Safety: operator hazards and overtopping safety of embankment and rockfill structures are listed issues
- Control restriction: entities controlled by China or a Chinese legal entity are not eligible
- Results: the granting authority may object to transfer or exclusive licensing of results for up to 4 years
- Satellite data: if used, Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS must be used
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Specific conditions and Scope

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
About 2 projects of around EUR 8.5 million each are expected, within a topic budget of EUR 17 million.
- Total project size: not stated
- Grant request: around EUR 8.5 million per project, for the whole consortium; other amounts may be requested and selected
- Funding form: lump sum (a fixed amount set from a detailed budget and paid against completed work packages)
Final budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 48–49 · Call ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-07), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Specific conditions
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — Budget flexibility

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Companies such as TenneT receive at most 70% of eligible costs; non-profit legal entities receive up to 100%.
- For-profit organisations: up to 70% of eligible costs, so at least 30% must come from their own resources
- Non-profit legal entities (for example universities and research organisations): up to 100% of eligible costs
- Co-financing conditions: the call sets no rule on cash or in-kind co-financing beyond the funding rate; the remainder is simply not reimbursed
Grants may not produce a profit: any surplus of revenue plus grant over costs is deducted from the final grant.
For lump sum grants the rate is applied when the lump sum is calculated and does not appear in the grant agreement.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 31–32 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
The grant is a lump sum fixed from a detailed budget table, which must still follow the normal cost-eligibility rules.
- Eligible costs: the detailed budget table must contain only costs that would be eligible under an actual-cost grant (personnel, subcontracting, purchases, other direct costs), because the lump sum must approximate the costs actually incurred
- Overheads and VAT: indirect costs are included in the lump sum calculation at the standard 25% flat rate of direct costs (excluding subcontracting)
- Subcontracting or equipment: purchases and subcontracting must give best value for money and be free of conflicts of interest; ineligible costs in the budget table can lead to a reduced grant, even late in the project
Payment depends on completing the work packages, not on proving the costs.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents, lump sum grant proposals
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 32 · G — Budget categories and cost eligibility rules

cards.title: Cash flow and financial exposure
cards.answer:
Partners normally receive a large advance after signing, minus a 5–8% contribution to a shared insurance fund, then interim payments.
- Payment model: pre-financing (an advance) of normally 160% of the average EU funding per reporting period, then interim payments linked to periodic reports, and a final payment after the final report fixes the grant
- Retention or guarantee: 5% to 8% of the maximum grant is deducted from the pre-financing and paid into the mutual insurance mechanism (a fund covering sums that cannot be recovered from beneficiaries)
- Financial reporting or audit: depending on grant size and type of beneficiary, a certificate on the financial statements may be required; each beneficiary is liable only for its own debts
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 32–33 · G — Reporting & payment arrangements, Certificates, Liability regime for recoveries

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: full proposals are due by 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time, through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal.
- Stage 1 — Full proposal: 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time; Part A online and Part B of at most 45 pages (the limit for lump sum innovation actions), with a detailed lump sum budget table
- Opening: 4 August 2027
- Additional procedure: none; the Commission may open the call up to one month earlier or later and delay the deadline by up to two months
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 48–49 · Call ENERGY (HORIZON-CL5-2027-07), Overview of this call
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The call sets no duration or start date: both are fixed in the grant agreement.
- Maximum duration: not set by the call; the grant agreement states the duration in months, and extensions are possible only exceptionally
- Required start: normally after the grant agreement is signed; an earlier start is possible only exceptionally, for duly justified reasons and with the granting authority's agreement
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 30–31 · G — Starting date & project duration

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Indicatively, the evaluation result comes about 5 months after the deadline and the grant agreement is signed about 8 months after it.
- Funding decision: about 5 months after the deadline (indicative), around May 2028
- Grant agreement: about 8 months after the deadline (indicative)
- Conditions before starting: an invitation to grant preparation is not yet a funding commitment, since legal entity validation, financial capacity and exclusion checks follow; the partners must sign a written consortium agreement
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 30 · F — Indicative timetable for evaluation and for signature of the grant agreement
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 29 · F — No commitment to provide funding
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Consortium agreement

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The proposal must be complete, submitted electronically before the deadline, and within the page limit; incomplete applications are rejected.
- Application form: Part A (administrative data and a summary budget, filled in online) and Part B (the technical description, uploaded as a PDF) through the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, using the forms inside the submission system; Part B is limited to 45 pages
- Budget: the summary budget in Part A and a detailed budget table, which is the basis for the lump sum
- Mandatory annexes: a plan for the exploitation and dissemination of results, including communication activities, and the ethics self-assessment
- Partner documents: the coordinator confirms at submission that it has the mandate to act for all applicants; every participant signs a declaration of honour before the grant is signed
- Registration: every beneficiary, affiliated entity and associated partner needs a participant identification code (PIC, a number from the EU Participant Register) before submission; validation of beneficiaries follows at grant preparation
- Parallel submission: none
- Lump sum: the detailed budget table is mandatory and is used to fix the lump sum
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 3–4 · A — Admissibility, Page limits
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 5 · B — Entities eligible to participate
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 15 · B — Ethics
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 27 · E — Documents
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 36 · IMPORTANT, Registration

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Independent experts score three criteria out of 5; a proposal needs 3 on each and 10 in total, and Impact weighs 1.5 times in the ranking.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (clear, ambitious objectives beyond the state of the art; sound methodology), Impact (credible pathways to the expected outcomes; dissemination and exploitation measures) and Quality and efficiency of the implementation (work plan, risks, resources, capacity of each partner)
- Thresholds: at least 3 out of 5 for each criterion and 10 out of 15 overall
- Weighting: for ranking, the Impact score counts 1.5 times
- Ranking rules: equal scores are separated first by whether a proposal covers aspects of the call not covered by higher-ranked ones, then by the Impact score, then Excellence, then gender balance among lead researchers and geographical diversity
- Budget assessment: the grant awarded may be lower than requested, and topic budgets may change by up to 20% after evaluation
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 23–26 · D — Award criteria, Scores and weighting, Two-stage calls
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · pp. 28–29 · F — Evaluation procedure and ranking, Budget flexibility
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, General Annexes · p. 31 · G — Form of grant, funding rate and maximum grant amount

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The lump sum, the China-control restriction, the ownership safeguard and the satellite-data rule apply in addition to the general rules.
- Exception — lump sum: the grant is fixed in advance from the detailed budget table
- Exception — entities controlled by China: not eligible
- Conditional — results transfer: the granting authority may object to transfers or exclusive licensing for 4 years after the project
- Conditional — satellite data: use Copernicus and/or Galileo/EGNOS if such data are used
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 143–144 · HORIZON-CL5-2027-07-D3-11, Specific conditions
